decision: The official-test signal is materially weaker than the earlier exposed-panel signal. The two RL seeds are coherent relative to c32 but exceed SFT by only one and three answers, with both descriptive RL-vs-SFT intervals spanning zero. Require a prospectively frozen replication to beat matched SFT without trading away World or Business accuracy before interpreting this as an RL-specific transfer benefit.
limits: Official-test examples are new local examples from AG News, not a new task or domain.
Absence from base-model pretraining is unknown.
The descriptive bootstrap unit is the shared four-record request, not 512 independent items.
Different results on exposed and official-test panels do not identify distribution-shift cause.
One favorable answer among fixed arms is not evidence that RL meaningfully beats SFT.
